messages:
Pranav: quick heads-up — I'm drafting an RFC for customer-managed on‑prem networking (VPC + onprem connector). Need alignment on scope and launch gating.
Maya: thanks — can you call out what customers pushed for vs what we want to ship first?
Pranav: yeah. Customer asks: BYO BGP peering, static egress IPs, KMS integration, and ability to route a subset of traffic to hosted fallback. Engineering constraints: we can't iterate on full BGP UI + robust NAT traversal in the same sprint.
Sam: high level tradeoff: BGP peering requires edge router config and testing permutations; NAT/static egress is faster but is operationally messier for customers (port mapping, double NAT).
Lina: security note — any onprem connector must support mTLS for control-plane + cert rotation hooks. Also audit logs forwarded to customer SIEM.
Jordan: from SEs — customers with strict compliance need deterministic egress IPs and a documented rollback path. They prefer BGP if we promise stability.
Pranav: proposed MVP scope in RFC: 1) connector agent (k8s + baremetal systemd) that establishes mTLS control plane, 2) support two egress modes: a) static NAT egress (fast path) b) passive BGP sessions (we don't originate, we accept route injection), 3) hosted fallback routing policy, 4) health & metrics export to Prometheus/Datadog.
Maya: sounds reasonable. What are the acceptance criteria? Need measurable gating for product/CS to sign off.
Pranav: draft acceptance criteria I put into the thread so we can iterate: 
`` 
Acceptance checklist (MVP):
- Customer can complete onboarding in <= 3 hours using instructions
- Control-plane connection established (mTLS) and agent shows READY
- Egress DNS/resolution from customer app -> external model endpoints verified
- Deterministic egress IP confirmed (static NAT) or announced prefix visible (passive BGP)
- Canary traffic (5% session-based) can be routed to private deployment and fall back without >200ms extra latency
- Audit logs delivered to customer SIEM within 60s
- Rollback: documented steps and automated route withdraw + switch to hosted model in <10min
```
Sam: a couple clarifications: what does "passive BGP" mean operationally? we need to decide if we accept route announcements only or also originate specific /32s. That affects kernel config and risk.
Pranav: MVP = accept announcements (no prefix origination). Stretch goal = managed prefix origination + rPKI checks.
Lina: add: TLS cert revocation path + JWK rotation for control plane. Also require FIPS-compliant crypto option for enterprise customers.
Jordan: CS asks that we include templated runbooks for customer network teams and a short checklist we can hand off during onboarding.
Maya: prioritization: we have limited cycles this quarter. Do we treat this as Dedicated-levelfeature or Private-P0? customers driving enterprise contracts should be P0 if revenue-impacting.
Sam: implementation notes from infra: 1) connector binary + helm chart 2) control-plane TLS termination in customer's VPC via 443/8443 3) egress handling: iptables MASQ for NAT path, bird for BGP passive path 4) observability endpoints /metrics and /healthz
Pranav: adding launch-risk matrix: 
- Risk: BGP misconfig -> traffic blackhole; Mitigation: staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%), automated health checks and immediate withdraw + notify customer.
- Risk: cert/rotation bug -> Mitigation: grace period + dual-key rollout, automated rollback.
- Risk: egress IP mismatch -> Mitigation: integration test harness + pre-onboard connectivity validation.
Maya: what's the estimated timeline? rough engineering estimate?
Sam: rough T-shirt: 6 weeks for agent + NAT egress + control-plane + basic observability. BGP passive + canary tooling additional 4 weeks. QA + docs 2 weeks. So end-to-end 12 weeks for full MVP if we parallelize.
Pranav: for prioritization: propose split into two deliverables so we can hit customers earlier: 
- Phase A (8w): agent + mTLS + static NAT egress + hosted-fallback + onboarding docs + runbooks + basic telemetry
- Phase B (4w): passive BGP, canary automation, enhanced rollback, SIEM integrations
Jordan: CS feedback: customers who asked will accept Phase A temporarily if we guarantee Phase B timeline and have a compensating SLA/credits clause. We should bake that into sales contracts.
Lina: compliance checklist: KMS key wrap for secrets in Phase A, option to integrate with customer's HSM in Phase B. Confirm with security.
Pranav: question for product: do we require a config UI for BGP (stretch) or just YAML + docs in v1?
Maya: start with YAML + docs; don't invest in UI until we see 3+ customers. Keep UI in backlog.
Sam: ops note — we need a route-validator service to detect accidental overlapping prefixes. Add to Phase B backlog if time permits.
ops-bot: deployment-note: nightly job will build connector images on merge to main; test clusters will run e2e connectivity daily. See: https://ci.redwood.example/org/connectors
Pranav: final ask: please react with :thumbsup: if you agree with phased delivery and the acceptance checklist above. If objections, reply with specifics. I'll fold comments into RFC and ping exec for prioritization tradeoff meeting.
Maya: :thumbsup: from product. I'll route to GTM for contract language.
Jordan: :thumbsup: from SE. I'll draft onboarding runbook template.
Lina: minor tweak: add FIPS flag in Phase A as opt-in. :thumbsup:
Sam: :thumbsup: engineering aligned. Let's make sure QA has environment parity notes.
Pranav: thanks all — I'll post the RFC link here once I convert this into the PRD + acceptance doc. Expect draft by EOD tomorrow.
Maya: cheers — also note: prioritize customers with existing contracts so Sales can close.
Jordan: logging task for SE: create two example customer configs (k8s + baremetal) and attach to RFC.
Pranav: noted — I'll tag you in the doc.
ops-bot: reminder: security review required before any customer pilot. Add label `security-review` to RFC PR.
Pranav: done. closing thread for now, will reopen with RFC link.
